one_month_reasoning: Window to 2026-11-29: (1) the reported Marvell-Lumentum all-stock deal could be announced 'as soon as mid next week' (CNBC); no 8-K or joint release by 2026-11-01. The stock already fell ~22% in two sessions, more than our estimate of what the deal costs holders if signed (~-$2.6 a share; -$10 on the harsher dis-synergy reading), so a deal near market is two-sided with a modest relief tilt; a richer premium or a long SAMR timeline is the downside. (2) Lumentum reports fiscal Q1 on Nov 5 (guide $1.225-1.275B), an industry read on laser demand. (3) NVIDIA's Q3 FY27 report (mid/late November) sets AI semis sentiment. Marvell's own Q3 FY27 report should fall in early December (Dec 2 last year), just outside the window. With no scheduled MRVL print and a two-sided deal event, we keep the round-1 near-symmetric lognormal: median ~$197 (+0.3%, a small reversal tilt) and sigma = 80%/3.5 = 22.9% for the month. Unchanged from round 1: no supervisor finding bears on the 1-month window.

downside.story: 10th percentile: AI capex 22% below the base path (toward the file low case: 2027 ~$1,390B, 2028 ~$1,265B) as lab/neocloud financing tightens; Marvell loses custom share (Trainium 3/4 at Alchip, an XPU programme slips) and LPO/CPO trims DSP content: share -10%; GM -1.5pt on deleverage; P/E -9 turns (~25x after SBC). Deal: signed at a richer premium with the Stifel-sized or larger DSP-customer backlash (V nearer -$10B than -$2.4B); the engine keeps the expected-value adjustment, the case's multiple carries the rest.

base.story: Median: AI capex on the standing file's base path (CY26 $1,225B -> CY27 $1,841B -> CY28 $2,255B); Marvell DC share 0.80% -> 0.92% -> 1.06% (custom ramp, scale-up optics, 1.6T DSPs, net of linear-drive pressure); FY28 revenue $19.1B (4.5% below the ~$20B outlook, 3% below Street), FY29 $26.3B (16% below MarketScreener); 34.2x after-SBC NTM P/E; Celestial earnout booked; Lumentum deal at expected value (p 0.585, -$2.63 a share if it happens: LITE valued on its own estimates roughly offsets the shares issued, the DSP dis-synergy is the net cost).

upside.story: 90th percentile: AI capex tracks the file's high path (2027 ~$2.2-2.4T) and Marvell hits the investor-day FY28 ~$20B and FY29 custom >$12B with scale-up optics ramping (share +7%); GM +0.5pt; P/E +6 turns. Deal: either walked away from (no dilution) or closed near market with laser-supply and CPO synergies and no material customer loss (V around +$5B).

thesis_break_reason: At $130 MRVL would trade ~16.5x our horizon NTM after-SBC EPS (~$7.9; ~13.9x on the peers' non-GAAP basis) and ~17.5x our FY28 non-GAAP EPS ($7.41), multiples NVDA/AVGO-type names only see when the market doubts the growth. Trading there would most likely mean the build is wrong in substance: a lost XPU programme or the custom ramp slipping a year, AI capex heading to the low case, or a signed Lumentum deal with a large DSP-customer backlash and a SAMR overhang. It sits roughly mid-way between spot and our $102 downside case. Round 1: $135; lowered with the $5 lower base and the smaller expected deal cost.

reverse_dcf_check: 34.2x after-SBC NTM EPS is a 2.9% earnings yield; with a ~10% cost of equity and ~80% payout capacity (fabless, capex ~3.5% of revenue) it implies ~7.6% perpetual growth after FY29, or roughly 18% EPS growth for five years after FY29 fading to GDP, with after-SBC operating margins held ~34-35% (Investor Day long-term non-GAAP 44-46% is above that); plausible only if AI data-center spend keeps compounding after 2028 and Marvell keeps its custom/optics share, which is why 1.5 turns come off for the long-dated risks and a normalised leg carries 25%.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set. Value is carried by a P/E horizon leg (weight 0.75) on the build's own after-SBC NTM EPS (Q4 FY28 + Q1-Q3 FY29) and a normalised-earnings custom leg (0.25; mid-cycle 28% after-SBC margin x 25x), per the semis playbook. Data Center revenue = customer AI capex (standing file base) x Marvell's share of it; communications a plain quarterly path; non-GAAP GM and opex drive EBIT, SBC is a cited constant subtracted (cost basis). Segment 'ebit' is gross profit allocated by revenue (Marvell reports one segment); opex + SBC sit in corporate_ebit. Adjustments: Celestial earnout liability (-749.5, p 1) and the Lumentum deal at expected value (V -2,412, p 0.585), both also deducted by hand inside the normalised leg because the engine adds adjustments only to multiple legs. No DCF leg (policy). Driven share of revenue: 100%. The normalised leg is not driver-linked (plain per-share value; scenarios move it via custom_pct).
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) Lumentum deal booked at p 0.585 (0.75 signed x 0.78 not blocked by the horizon); V -2.4B rests on LITE valued on its own estimates (15% haircut, 31.9x) and a -5B DSP dis-synergy smaller than the supervisor's -8B because the two largest module makers already run on Broadcom DSPs (PhotonCap); at -8B the target falls ~$1.3. (2) Normalised leg (25x on 28% after-SBC margin) is judgment; at 30x it adds ~+$8 (+3%). (3) The 1.5-turn long-dated-risk haircut on the exit P/E is judgment (~-4%). (4) After-SBC conversion 1.19 is from the build's own horizon NTM; the Street/Zacks ratio 1.214 would add ~2%. (5) Shares now move by buybacks and Google warrant shares only (-0.25%/yr); SBC is costed so its issuance is not added. (6) No other financing event >= 20%: the deal is all-stock (no debt raise reported); the $3B revolver (8-K 2026-10-23) is undrawn.

model_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 34.2x after-SBC NTM EPS is a 2.9% earnings yield; with a ~10% cost of equity and ~80% payout capacity (fabless, capex ~3.5% of revenue) it implies ~7.6% perpetual growth after FY29, or roughly 18% EPS growth for five years after FY29 fading to GDP, with after-SBC operating margins held ~34-35% (Investor Day long-term non-GAAP 44-46% is above that); plausible only if AI data-center spend keeps compounding after 2028 and Marvell keeps its custom/optics share, which is why 1.5 turns come off for the long-dated risks and a normalised leg carries 25%.

reasoning: Round 2. Standalone first: the quarterly driver build is unchanged in its DC engine (customer AI capex from the standing file base x Marvell share 0.80% -> 0.92% -> 1.06%, checked against industry evidence: LightCounting DSP data, Coherent InP capacity doubling, TrendForce 800G+ transceivers 24M -> 63M in 2026, Broadcom AI +221%), giving FY27 $12.0B / FY28 $19.1B / FY29 $26.3B revenue; communications trimmed. Non-GAAP EPS FY27 4.25 / FY28 7.41 sits at the Street (4.22 / 7.33) and at the whisper (~4.26 / ~7.40, Street + Marvell's ~1% habitual beat); FY29 revenue is 16% under MarketScreener's $31.3B because we do not assume the full custom share gain. Supervisor findings acted on: (a) Celestial earnout liability -749.5 added (missed in round 1); (b) peer median 30.15x on 8 whole-company peers (LITE, RMBS dropped); (c) the after-SBC conversion now uses the build's own NTM ratio 1.19 instead of a Street/Zacks mix; (d) share count now moves by buybacks and non-SBC warrant shares only (-0.25%/yr) with shareholder returns cut to match buyback cash (round 1 took 1.8-2.5B a year out of the bridge without retiring shares); (e) Lumentum valued on its own estimates (MarketScreener net income, NTM 32.3x today, exit 31.9x, 15% haircut) rather than MRVL's growth factor; (f) a DSP dis-synergy added. Where I differ: my dis-synergy is -5B, not -8B, because industry sources show Innolight/Eoptolink already use Broadcom's DSP and Marvell's sockets are hyperscaler-specified; and p is 0.585 (I weight CNBC's independent timetable more). Result: P/E leg 34.2x x ~$7.9 = $272.18 (w 0.75), normalised $157.94 (w 0.25), research target (12m) $243.62 (round 1 $247.70: lower multiple base and Celestial, partly offset by a much smaller deal cost, -$1.54 vs -$6.5 a share). Downside case $102.25 and upside case $400.17 move the drivers (capex -22%/+20%, share -10%/+7%, GM) and the multiple; the left tail stays fatter. Thesis break $130. 1-month ladder unchanged: deal news and LITE/NVDA prints are two-sided. Research in round 2 was 6 searches/fetches (deal status, LITE results and estimates, optical DSP industry structure).
